acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Rotwalkers family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Plague Lord, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Cathedral-of-Corpses Sovereign (Sovereign) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: A cathedral-like architecture of individually readable fused bodies centered on one grinning face, draped in stitched shrouds, veiled by a directed haze of flies, and seated on a throne whose four corpse aisles can visibly tear away.

Signature mechanic: Throne of the Dead: four stitched-shroud aisles radiate from the Lord's fused-body throne. The Foot aisle assembles a Shambler and stores a fall lane; the Hand aisle cords a surviving corpse into a Ghoul; the Rib aisle pressurizes all connected trails through a Rot Brute; and the Many aisle folds two disabled bodies into an Amalgam. The central grinning face exhales a fly column toward one aisle while its corpses tighten that aisle's great suture. Cutting the exposed suture permanently collapses that production and tears one structural body from the throne. After two aisles fall, the remaining corpses unfold as mismatched limbs around the central body, which cycles only surviving commands and loses one limb whenever its matching aisle is destroyed.
battlefieldDuty: Rule a stitched-shroud boss arena that produces lower Rotwalkers, routes their death trails through four corpse aisles, and progressively transforms its throne into a mobile but mechanically simpler central body.
constructionDimensions: Corpse anatomy becomes a pressure bellows through hollow exposed ribs, vane-like burial strips, dried tendon sails, whistle gaps in bone blades, and on T4–T5 distinct head-and-torso vents that preserve every component body.

Motion gains directional articulation through cloth pull, fly-stream alignment, rib compression, asymmetric limb lift, and a visible still pocket behind the dislocated joint or central face anchoring the gust.
counterplay: Follow the fly column, interrupt or displace the lower form feeding the selected aisle, cut the taut great suture during production, and use each collapsed aisle as clean ground; every destroyed aisle permanently removes a command, a throne support, and one later transformation limb. Affinity signal: Ribs compress and burial strips snap flat before a pressure action while one wrong-angled joint remains still; entering that lee or striking the still anchor collapses the gust-assisted motion.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only wind treatment without bellows anatomy, directional cloth, and changed articulation
Glow-only wind treatment without force direction or a still anchor
Transparency that removes wet flesh, exposed sinew, or component corpse readability
Omnidirectional debris or flies that obscure the loaded body and counterplay seam
identityInvariants: A recognizably human but wrong silhouette retains dislocated shoulders, a dragging or mismatched gait, a hanging jaw, and a head or torso held at an impossible angle.
Grey-green and bruise-purple flesh, dried-blood brown, bile yellow, and dirty linen white remain bodily and funerary rather than elemental colors.
Rotting flesh, exposed sinew, wet bone, grave dirt, torn burial clothing, and the visible marks or embedded tools of death preserve each corpse's material history.
Every form is wet and partly open, with readable seams at tendons, ribs, sutures, or fused bodies that explain both animation and counterplay.
Escalation reverses decay into coordination: sagging fragments become corded muscle, reinforced bone, cooperative corpse anatomy, and finally a plague court built from many still-legible bodies.
telegraph: The stitched shrouds lift toward one aisle, flies stream in a single readable column, the central grin turns to the matching corpse arch, and its great wet suture pulls taut before bodies begin moving.
